answer: It includes Company Non-Elective Contributions, DC SERP Contributions, and historic Executive SSP+ Company Contributions.

question: What is the purpose of the DCP Accounts component of the Executive Supplemental Savings Plan?
answer: DCP Accounts are the recordkeeping accounts established for Participants who participated in the Deferred Compensation Plan for Employees of The Boeing Company, which was frozen December 31, 2018 and merged into this Plan effective January 1, 2022.

question: When was the Executive Supplemental Savings Plan originally established?
answer: Effective January 1, 1978.

question: When was the Executive Supplemental Savings Plan last amended and restated to comply with Code section 409A?
answer: January 1, 2008.

question: What changes were made to the Executive Supplemental Savings Plan as of January 1, 2022?
answer: (A) Reflect the merger of the Deferred Compensation Plan for Employees of The Boeing Company with and into the Plan, (B) eliminate Restoration SSP+ Company Contributions and Executive SSP+ Company Contributions, (C) add a new Restoration True-Up Contribution, Incentive Matching Contribution and Company Non-Elective Contribution, (D) simplify the mid-year enrollment provisions in the Participant Deferral component of the Plan, and (E) make certain other changes.

question: What is the status of the Executive Supplemental Savings Plan under Code section 409A?
answer: The Plan is a nonqualified deferred compensation plan subject to Code section 409A.

question: What is the intended status of the Plan under section 3(36) of ERISA?
answer: The Plan is intended to be, in part, an excess benefit plan as defined in section 3(36) of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended, to the extent benefits are paid in excess of the limits imposed by Code section 415.

question: What is the intended status of the Plan under sections 201(2), 301(a)(3), and 401(a)(1) of ERISA if it is not an excess benefit plan?
answer: The Plan is intended to be an unfunded plan maintained primarily for the purpose of providing deferred compensation to a select group of management or highly compensated employees.

question: What is the definition of "Account" in the Executive Supplemental Savings Plan?
answer: “Account” means the recordkeeping account established for each Participant, for purposes of accounting for the allocations made hereunder and the Earnings Credits thereon.

question: What are the sub-accounts that make up an Account in the Executive Supplemental Savings Plan?
answer: (a) the Restoration Account, (b) the Extra Deferral Account, (c) the Executive Benefit Account, and (d) the DCP Account.

question: Who is the Administrator of the Executive Supplemental Savings Plan?
answer: The Employee Benefit Plans Committee of The Boeing Company.

question: What is the definition of "Affiliate or Subsidiary" in the Executive Supplemental Savings Plan?
answer: A member of a controlled group of corporations (as defined in Code section 1563(a), determined without regard to Code sections 1563(a)(4) and (e)(3)(c)), a group of trades or businesses (whether incorporated or not) which are under common control within the meaning of Code section 414(c), or an affiliated service group (as defined in Code sections 414(m) or 414(o)), in each case of which The Boeing Company is a part.

question: What is the definition of "Authorized Period of Absence" in the Executive Supplemental Savings Plan?
answer: A leave of absence approved by the Company.

question: What is the definition of "Base Pay" in the Executive Supplemental Savings Plan?
answer: An Employee’s base pay (salary) from the Company, determined without regard to the limitation on such compensation under Code section 401(a)(17) and prior to any deferrals of compensation made hereunder.

question: What does "Base Pay" not include according to the document?
answer: Payments under any incentive compensation or performance award plan.

question: What is the definition of "Base Pay Deferrals" in the Executive Supplemental Savings Plan?
answer: Deferrals of Base Pay that are made pursuant to Section 3.1(A).

question: What is the definition of "Base Pay Rate" in the Executive Supplemental Savings Plan?
answer: An Employee’s annual rate of Base Pay.

question: What is the definition of "Beneficiary" in the Executive Supplemental Savings Plan?
answer: The person or persons designated by a Participant to receive distributions from the Plan upon the Participant’s death, in accordance with the rules established by the Administrator.

question: What is the definition of "Board of Directors" in the Executive Supplemental Savings Plan?
answer: The board of directors of The Boeing Company.

question: What is the definition of "Boeing 401(k)" in the Executive Supplemental Savings Plan?
answer: The Boeing Company 401(k) Retirement Plan, as amended.

question: What is the definition of "BSS Plan" in the Executive Supplemental Savings Plan?
answer: The BSS Retirement Plan, as amended.

question: What is the definition of "Cash Incentive" in the Executive Supplemental Savings Plan?
answer: The amount awarded to the Participant under The Boeing Company Elected Officer Annual Incentive Plan or The Boeing Company Annual Incentive Plan.

question: What happens to a Cash Incentive deferred by a Participant for purposes of calculating Company Non-Elective Contributions?
answer: It is deemed to have been paid as if those amounts had not been deferred.

question: What happens to a Cash Incentive paid after a Participant’s termination of employment from the Controlled Group?
answer: It remains subject to the Participant’s deferral election under Article III if it has become irrevocable under Section 3.3(c) as of the Participant’s termination.

question: What does “Board of Directors” mean in the document?
answer: “Board of Directors” means the board of directors of The Boeing Company.

question: What does “Boeing 401(k)” mean in the document?
answer: “Boeing 401(k)” means The Boeing Company 401(k) Retirement Plan, as amended.

question: What does “BSS Plan” mean in the document?
answer: “BSS Plan” means the BSS Retirement Plan, as amended.

question: What does “Cash Incentive” mean in the document?
answer: “Cash Incentive” means the amount awarded to the Participant under The Boeing Company Elected Officer Annual Incentive Plan or The Boeing Company Annual Incentive Plan (formerly the Incentive Compensation Plan for Employees of The Boeing Company and Subsidiaries).

question: What does “Cash Incentive Deferrals” mean in the document?
answer: “Cash Incentive Deferrals” means deferrals of Cash Incentive that are made pursuant to Section 3.1(A).

question: What does “Code” mean in the document?
answer: “Code” means the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended. Any reference to a specific provision of the Code includes any successor provision thereto and the regulations and rulings promulgated thereunder.

question: What does “Company” mean in the document?
answer: “Company” means The Boeing Company, its successors in interest, and any Affiliate or Subsidiary that has adopted this Plan with the consent of The Boeing Company. An Affiliate or Subsidiary is deemed to have adopted this Plan, and The Boeing Company is deemed to have consented to such adoption, if the Affiliate or Subsidiary (a) participates in the Boeing 401(k) and (b) is not an excluded employer for purposes of this Plan. A list of excluded employers, as updated from time to time, is attached hereto as Appendix A.

question: What does “Company Contributions” mean in the document?
answer: “Company Contributions” mean Restoration Matching Contributions, Restoration True-Up Contributions, Company Non-Elective Contributions, Incentive Matching Contributions, and DC SERP Contributions. For periods prior to January 1, 2022, Company Contributions also included Restoration SSP+ Company Contributions and Executive SSP+ Company Contributions.

question: What does “Company Non-Elective Contributions” mean in the document?
answer: “Company Non-Elective Contributions” mean the contributions allocated pursuant to Section 4.4.

question: What does “Compensation” mean in the document?
answer: “Compensation” means a Participant’s Base Pay, Cash Incentive, and Performance Awards, if any.

question: What does “Compensation Committee” mean in the document?
answer: “Compensation Committee” means the Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors.

question: What does “Contribution Credit” mean in the document?
answer: “Contribution Credit” means the applicable percentage used to compute an eligible Participant’s DC SERP Contributions under Section 4.5.

question: What does “Controlled Group” mean in the document?
answer: “Controlled Group” means the Company and any Affiliate or Subsidiary.

question: What does “DC SERP Contributions” mean in the document?
answer: “DC SERP Contributions” mean the contributions allocated pursuant to Section 4.5.

question: What does “Deferral Election” mean in the document?
answer: “Deferral Election” means the elections made by an Eligible Employee to defer a portion of his or her eligible Compensation in accordance with Article III, including any Restoration Deferral Election and any Extra Deferral Election.

question: What does “DCP” mean in the document?
answer: “DCP” means the Deferred Compensation Plan for Employees of The Boeing Company, which was merged into this Plan effective January 1, 2022.

question: What does “DCP Deferrals” mean in the document?
answer: “DCP Deferrals” mean the portion of a Participant’s Base Pay, Cash Incentive, or Performance Awards, if any, that he or she elected to defer on a pre-tax basis under the DCP prior to January 1, 2019.

question: What does “DCP Matching Contributions” mean in the document?
answer: “DCP Matching Contributions” mean the matching contributions that were previously made under the DCP.

question: What does “Earnings Credits” mean in the document?
answer: “Earnings Credits” means the adjustment to a Participant’s Account under Section 7.2, which may be positive or negative.

question: What does “Election Period” mean in the document?
answer: “Election Period” means the period or periods established by the Administrator during which an eligible Employee may submit Deferral Elections, all in accordance with such timing and other requirements as the Administrator may establish and, in all cases, the applicable rules under Code section 409A. In no event will (a) an annual Election Period for Participant Deferrals other than Cash Incentive Deferrals expire later than December 31 of the Plan Year in which the election is made, (b) an annual Election Period for Cash Incentive Deferrals expire later than March 30 of the Plan Year to which the election relates (or such other date that is immediately prior to the date that the related Cash Incentive has become “readily ascertainable” as determined in accordance with Treas. Regs. Section 1.409A-2(a)(8)), and/or (c) a mid-year Election Period expire more than thirty (30) days after the Employee first becomes eligible to participate in the Plan.

question: What does “Eligibility Determination Date” mean in the document?
answer: “Eligibility Determination Date” means (a) for purposes of Participant Deferrals other than Cash Incentive Deferrals with respect to any Plan Year, the November 1 of the preceding Plan Year (or such other date as determined by the Administrator with respect to any Employee(s); provided that such determination complies with the requirements of Code section 409A), (b) for purposes of Cash Incentive Deferrals made with respect to any Cash Incentive earned in any Plan Year beginning on and after January 1, 2023, the March 1 of the Plan Year to which the Deferral Election relates (or such other date as determined by the Administrator with respect to any Employee(s); provided that such determination complies with the requirements of Code section 409A), and (c) for purposes of the definition of “Newly Eligible,” the date an Eligible Employee is hired or rehired into the status of an Eligible Employee. For the 2022 Plan Year, November 1, 2021 was used as the default Eligibility Determination Date for all 2022 full Plan Year Deferral Elections.

question: What does “Eligible Employee” mean in the document?
answer: “Eligible Employee” means, with respect to any Plan Year (or portion of a Plan Year, in the case of a mid-year enrollment) if applicable, an individual who is an Employee and is paid on a U.S. dollar-based payroll as of the Eligibility Determination Date, and who has satisfied any additional requirements to make Extra Deferrals under Section 3.1(A) or 3.2, to make Restoration Deferrals under Section 3.1(B) or 3.2, to receive allocations of Restoration Matching Contributions under Section 4.1, to receive allocations of Restoration True-Up Contributions under Section 4.2, to receive allocations of Incentive Matching Contributions under Section 4.3, to receive allocations of Company Non-Elective Contributions under Section 4.4, and/or to receive allocations of DC SERP Contributions under Section 4.5, in each case, if any and to the extent applicable. Notwithstanding the foregoing or anything herein: (i) an Employee is an Eligible Employee only if the Employee is eligible for the Boeing 401(k), and is not eligible for The Boeing Company Supplemental Savings Plan and (ii) an Employee shall not be considered an Eligible Employee hereunder if the Administrator has excluded his or her employer from participation in the Plan. A list of excluded employers, as updated from time to time, is attached hereto as Appendix A.

question: What does “Employee” mean in the document?
answer: “Employee” means any person who is employed by any member of the Controlled Group, is designated as a common law employee on such member’s payroll, and is assigned by such member to the US Executive Payroll.

question: What does “Extra Deferrals” mean in the document?
answer: “Extra Deferrals” means any Base Pay Deferral, Cash Incentive Deferral or Vested Performance Award Deferral that a Participant elects to defer on a pre-tax basis in accordance with Section 3.1(A) and, to the extent applicable, Section 3.2(A).

question: What does “Executive SSP+ Company Contributions” mean in the document?
answer: “Executive SSP+ Company Contributions” means the historic Executive SSP+ Company Contributions that were credited to a Participant’s Account with respect to periods prior to January 1, 2022.

question: What does “Incentive Matching Contributions” mean in the document?
answer: “Incentive Matching Contributions” mean the contributions allocated pursuant to Section 4.3.

question: What does “Newly Eligible” mean in the document?
answer: “Newly Eligible” means an individual who (i) is hired or rehired as an Employee, (ii) was not eligible to participate in the Plan or in a deferred compensation plan that is aggregated with the Plan under the aggregation rules of Code section 409A (including The Boeing Company Supplemental Savings Plan), other than the crediting of earnings, within the 24-month period immediately preceding the Eligibility Determination Date (or, has taken a full distribution of his or her interest in such plan), and (iii) is paid on a U.S. dollar-based payroll as of the Eligibility Determination Date.

question: What does “Participant” mean in the document?
answer: “Participant” means an Eligible Employee who has elected to defer Compensation or who is eligible to receive a Company Contribution hereunder, or for purposes of Articles V through X, an Employee or former Employee who has amounts credited to his or her Account.

question: What does “Participant Deferrals” mean in the document?
answer: “Participant Deferrals” mean Extra Deferrals and Restoration Deferrals.

question: What does “Performance Awards” mean in the document?
answer: “Performance Awards” means any award designated as such under The Boeing Company’s 2003 Incentive Stock Plan and any successor or other long-term equity incentive plan that may be maintained by The Boeing Company from time to time.

question: What does “Plan” mean in the document?
answer: “Plan” means The Boeing Company Executive Supplemental Savings Plan as herein set forth, together with any amendments that may be adopted from time to time.

question: What does “Plan Year” mean in the document?
answer: “Plan Year” means the calendar year.

question: What does “PVP” mean in the document?
answer: “PVP” means The Pension Value Plan for Employees of The Boeing Company, as amended.

question: What does “Restoration Deferrals” mean in the document?
answer: “Restoration Deferrals” mean the portion of a Participant’s Compensation, if any, that he or she elects to defer on a pre-tax basis under this Plan in accordance with Section 3.1(B) and, to the extent applicable, Section 3.2.

question: What does “Restoration Matching Contributions” mean in the document?
answer: “Restoration Matching Contributions” mean the amount credited to a Participant’s Account under Section 4.1.

question: What does “Restoration SSP+ Company Contributions” mean in the document?
answer: “Restoration SSP+ Company Contributions” means the historic Restoration SSP+ Company Contributions that were credited to a Participant’s Account with respect to periods prior to January 1, 2022.

question: What does “Restoration True-Up Contributions” mean in the document?
answer: “Restoration True-Up Contributions” mean the contributions allocated pursuant to Section 4.2.

question: What does “Separation from Service” mean in the document?
answer: “Separation from Service” or “Separates from Service” means an Employee’s death, retirement or termination of employment from the Controlled Group within the meaning of Code section 409A. For purposes of determining whether a Separation from Service has occurred, Affiliates and Subsidiaries are defined by using the language “at least 80 percent” to define the controlled group under Code section 1563(a) in lieu of the 50 percent default rule stated in Treasury Regulation section 1.409A-1(h)(3). A Separation from Service is deemed to include a reasonably anticipated permanent reduction in the level of services performed by an Employee to less than 50 percent of the average level of services performed by the Employee during the immediately preceding 36-month period.

question: What does “Service” mean in the document?
answer: “Service” means the Participant’s years of service with the Controlled Group, determined in the same manner as the service time calculation under the Boeing Service Awards Program procedure, in completed whole years.

question: What does “Specified Employee” mean in the document?
answer: “Specified Employee” means an Employee who is a “specified employee” within the meaning of Code section 409A. Specified Employee status is determined on the last day of the prior Plan Year, to take effect as of April 1 of the Plan Year for a 12-month period. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Specified Employees shall be determined by including the employees who are reasonably determined to be the 75 top-paid officers of the Controlled Group as of the determination date, rather than the 50 top-paid officers as provided under Code section 416(i)(1)(A), to the extent permitted under Code section 409A.

question: What does “Unforeseeable Emergency” mean in the document?
answer: “Unforeseeable Emergency” means “unforeseeable emergency” within the meaning of Code section 409A, as determined by the Administrator.

question: What does “US Executive Payroll” mean in the document?
answer: “US Executive Payroll” means the executive designation of level EL, EV or ED at the Company (prior to August 15, 2022, the executive designation of level E-1 to E-5 at the Company). The US Executive Payroll was previously called the “E-Series Payroll.”

question: What does “Vested Performance Award Deferrals” mean in the document?
answer: “Vested Performance Award Deferrals” means deferrals of Performance Awards under Section 3.1(A).

question: What does the Plan provide for Eligible Employees in terms of deferral options?
answer: The Plan provides Eligible Employees with two ways to defer Compensation on a pre-tax basis– the Extra Deferral component and the Restoration Deferral component.

question: What is the maximum percentage of Base Pay that an Eligible Employee can defer as an Extra Deferral?
answer: An Eligible Employee may elect to defer up to 50% of his or her Base Pay payable in the Plan Year to which the Deferral Election applies as an Extra Deferral.

question: What is the maximum percentage of Cash Incentive that an Eligible Employee can defer as an Extra Deferral?
answer: An Eligible Employee may elect to defer 100% of his or her Cash Incentive earned in the Plan Year to which the Deferral Election relates as an Extra Deferral.

question: What is the maximum percentage of Vested Performance Awards that an Eligible Employee can defer as an Extra Deferral?
answer: An Eligible Employee may elect to defer 100% of his or her Performance Awards granted in the Plan Year to which the Deferral Election applies as an Extra Deferral.

question: What is the maximum percentage of Base Pay that an Eligible Employee can defer as a Restoration Deferral?
answer: An Eligible Employee may elect a deferral percentage up to the maximum percentage of his or her Base Pay that the Employee can elect to contribute on a pre-tax, after-tax and/or Roth basis under the Boeing 401(k).

question: When are Restoration Deferrals made from Base Pay?
answer: Restoration Deferrals will be made from the Eligible Employee’s Base Pay only after either: (1) Base Pay for the applicable Plan Year reaches the limitation under Code section 401(a)(17), as indexed, for such Plan Year or (2) the Participant’s annual additions under the Boeing 401(k) for the applicable Plan Year reach the dollar limitation of Code section 415(c), as indexed.

question: When are Participant Deferrals credited to the Participant’s Account?
answer: Extra Deferrals will be credited to the Participant’s Account on the date the Compensation would otherwise be payable, or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible.

question: When can mid-year elections for Extra Deferrals be made?
answer: An Employee who is Newly Eligible during a Plan Year may elect Extra Deferrals up to a maximum of 50% of the Base Pay earned and payable in each full regular pay period commencing after the end of the Election Period (or such other date determined by the Administrator in accordance with Code section 409A) for the remainder of the applicable Plan Year.

question: Can mid-year elections be made for Cash Incentive Deferrals or Vested Performance Award Deferrals?
answer: Mid-year elections cannot be made for Cash Incentive Deferrals or Vested Performance Award Deferrals.

question: What is the default Eligibility Determination Date for the 2022 Plan Year?
answer: For the 2022 Plan Year, November 1, 2021 was used as the default Eligibility Determination Date for all 2022 full Plan Year Deferral Elections.

question: What is the definition of a “Newly Eligible” individual?
answer: “Newly Eligible” means an individual who (i) is hired or rehired as an Employee, (ii) was not eligible to participate in the Plan or in a deferred compensation plan that is aggregated with the Plan under the aggregation rules of Code section 409A (including The Boeing Company Supplemental Savings Plan), other than the crediting of earnings, within the 24-month period immediately preceding the Eligibility Determination Date (or, has taken a full distribution of his or her interest in such plan), and (iii) is paid on a U.S. dollar-based payroll as of the Eligibility Determination Date.

question: What is the definition of a “Specified Employee”?
answer: “Specified Employee” means an Employee who is a “specified employee” within the meaning of Code section 409A. Specified Employee status is determined on the last day of the prior Plan Year, to take effect as of April 1 of the Plan Year for a 12-month period. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Specified Employees shall be determined by including the employees who are reasonably determined to be the 75 top-paid officers of the Controlled Group as of the determination date, rather than the 50 top-paid officers as provided under Code section 416(i)(1)(A), to the extent permitted under Code section 409A.

question: What is the date on which the Boeing 401(k) plan was amended and restated?
answer: January 1, 2019

question: What is the maximum percentage of Base Pay that an Employee can elect to contribute on a pre-tax, after-tax, and/or Roth basis under the Boeing 401(k)?
answer: The maximum percentage of his or her Base Pay that the Employee can elect to contribute

question: What is the condition for making a Restoration Deferral Election under the Boeing 401(k)?
answer: An Eligible Employee must make a timely Restoration Deferral Election, as described in Section 3.3, to become eligible to participate in the Restoration Matching Contribution component of the Plan

question: What is the condition for making a Cash Incentive Deferral Election under the Boeing 401(k)?
answer: An Eligible Employee must make a timely Cash Incentive Deferral Election, as described in Section 3.3, to become eligible for the related Incentive Matching Contributions

question: What is the condition for receiving a Restoration True-Up Contribution under the Boeing 401(k)?
answer: The Employee must otherwise satisfy the eligibility requirements for a true-up matching contribution in the Boeing 401(k)

question: What is the condition for receiving a Company Non-Elective Contribution under the Boeing 401(k)?
answer: An Eligible Employee for purposes of this Section 4.4 need not make (or be eligible to make) deferrals to the Plan in order to receive an allocation of Company Non-Elective Contributions for such Plan Year

question: What is the amount of the Company Non-Elective Contribution for Plan Years beginning January 1, 2022 and January 1, 2023?
answer: A contribution equal to 2% of the Eligible Employee’s Base Pay and Cash Incentive paid by the Company during the applicable Plan Year

question: What is the condition for receiving DC SERP Contributions under the Boeing 401(k)?
answer: An Employee is eligible to receive DC SERP Contributions with respect to a Plan Year for so long as he or she satisfies the conditions in either (i) or (ii) below

question: What is the date range for employees hired between January 1, 2009 and December 31, 2019 to be eligible for DC SERP Contributions?
answer: The Employee was hired on or after January 1, 2009, but before January 1, 2020

question: What is the level requirement for employees hired between January 1, 2009 and December 31, 2019 to be eligible for DC SERP Contributions?
answer: The Employee is on the US Executive Payroll in level EL or EV (referred to as level E-1, E-2, or E-3 prior to August 15, 2022), and was on the US Executive Payroll (in any level E-1 through E-5) as of December 31, 2019

question: What is the condition for employees hired before January 1, 2009 to be eligible for DC SERP Contributions?
answer: The Employee was hired before January 1, 2009, and was on the US Executive Payroll (in any level E-1 through E-5) as of December 31, 2019

question: What is the condition for employees to be ineligible to accrue benefits under any defined benefit plan maintained by the Controlled Group?
answer: The Employee is ineligible to accrue benefits under any defined benefit plan maintained by the Controlled Group

question: What is the condition for employees to not be elected officers of the Company to be eligible for DC SERP Contributions?
answer: The Employee is not an elected officer of the Company

question: What is the condition for a transfer of employment among members of the Controlled Group to not be considered a rehire?
answer: A transfer of employment among members of the Controlled Group, without interruption, is not considered a rehire

question: What is the condition for a rehire to the Controlled Group following a termination of employment due to layoff to not be treated as a rehire?
answer: A rehire to the Controlled Group following a termination of employment due to layoff generally will not be treated as a rehire, if rehire occurs within six years of the layoff event

question: What is the condition for a laid off Employee who commences a retirement benefit during a six-year period to be treated as a rehire?
answer: A laid off Employee who commences a retirement benefit during this six-year period will be treated as a rehire if he or she later rehires to the Controlled Group

question: What is the definition of a “group-acquired employee” for purposes of determining eligibility to receive a contribution for periods on and after January 1, 2009?
answer: An employee of the Company who became such as an immediate or ultimate result of a merger to which the Company was a party, or of the acquisition by the Company of all or part of another company

question: What is the date on which an individual who became a “group-acquired employee” after September 30, 2008 and before January 1, 2009 will be deemed to have been hired?
answer: An individual who became a “group-acquired employee” after September 30, 2008 and before January 1, 2009 will be deemed to have been hired on or after January 1, 2009

question: What is the date on which no contribution will be paid for a group-acquired employee?
answer: No contribution will be paid prior to January 1, 2009

question: What is the condition for a return to the Controlled Group directly from an approved leave of absence to not be considered a rehire?
answer: A return to the Controlled Group directly from an approved leave of absence, without incurring a termination of employment, is not considered a rehire

question: What is the condition for a period of employment with ULA or USA to be considered an approved leave of absence?
answer: An Employee’s period of employment with ULA or USA will be considered an approved leave of absence, to the extent that the Employee first transferred directly from the Controlled Group to ULA or USA and subsequently transferred directly from ULA or USA back to the Controlled Group

question: What is the condition for a transfer of employment among members of the Controlled Group to not be considered a rehire?
answer: A transfer of employment among members of the Controlled Group, without interruption, is not considered a rehire

question: What is the condition for a Company Non-Elective Contribution to not be made if an Eligible Employee terminates from employment prior to the last business day of the Plan Year?
answer: The Company Non-Elective Contribution will not be made if the Eligible Employee terminates from employment prior to the last business day of the Plan Year for any reason other than retirement (for this purpose, after attaining age 55 with 10 years of service or after attaining age 62 with 1 year of service), disability (for this purpose, meaning the Eligible Employee is determined to be disabled by the Social Security Administration), layoff, or death

question: What is the condition for a Cash Incentive to not be counted for purposes of calculating the Company Non-Elective Contribution?
answer: Cash Incentive that is paid after an Eligible Employee’s termination of employment from the Controlled Group will not be counted for purposes of calculating the Company Non-Elective Contribution

question: What is the condition for a Company Non-Elective Contribution to be credited to an Eligible Employee’s Account?
answer: A Company Non-Elective Contribution will be credited to the Eligible Employee’s Account on the date the related non-elective contribution is made to the Boeing 401(k) (if any) or on the date otherwise determined by the Compensation Committee or its delegates, or, in each case, as soon thereafter as administratively feasible

question: What is the condition for a Restoration True-Up Contribution to be credited to a Participant’s Account?
answer: The Restoration True-Up Contribution, if any, will be credited to the Participant’s Account on the date that true-up matching contributions are made to the Boeing 401(k), or as soon as thereafter administratively feasible

question: What is the condition for an Incentive Matching Contribution to be credited to a Participant’s Account?
answer: Incentive Matching Contributions will be credited to the Participant’s Account on the date that the underlying Cash Incentive Deferrals are credited to the Participant’s Account

question: What is the condition for an Incentive Matching Contribution to not be made with respect to any Cash Incentive?
answer: No Incentive Matching Contribution will be made with respect to any Cash Incentive that is paid (or, but for the Participant’s Cash Incentive Deferral election, would be paid) after the date the Participant terminates from employment

question: What is the condition for a Restoration Matching Contribution to be credited to a Participant’s Account?
answer: Restoration Matching Contributions will be credited to the Participant’s Account on the date that the underlying Restoration Deferrals are credited to the Participant’s Account

question: What is the condition for a Restoration Matching Contribution to be made?
answer: A Participant who defers Base Pay pursuant to a Restoration Deferral Election under Section 3.3 will be credited with a Restoration Matching Contribution from the Company related to such Restoration Deferrals

question: What is the condition for a Restoration Matching Contribution to not be made?
answer: Restoration Matching Contributions will not be made with respect to Participant Deferrals of Base Pay made pursuant to an Extra Deferral Election

question: What is the condition for a Restoration True-Up Contribution to not be made?
answer: No Restoration True-Up Contribution will be made if the Employee terminates from employment prior to the last business day of the Plan Year for any reason other than retirement (for this purpose, after attaining age 55 with 10 years of service or after attaining age 62 with 1 year of service), disability (for this purpose, meaning the Eligible Employee is determined to be disabled by the Social Security Administration), layoff, or death

question: What is the condition for a Restoration True-Up Contribution to not exceed 100% of the first 10% of eligible compensation?
answer: In no event shall the Restoration True-Up Contribution for a Plan Year, if any, when added to the matching contributions to the Boeing 401(k) (including true-up matching contributions) and any Restoration Matching Contributions made for such Plan Year, exceed 100% of the first 10% of eligible compensation contributed or credited to the Boeing 401(k) and this Plan

question: What is the condition for a Deferral Election to become irrevocable for a full Plan Year?
answer: Deferral Elections with respect to a full Plan Year (including Cash Incentive Deferral Elections) will generally become irrevocable as of the date established by the Administrator, which in all cases shall be no later than the dates prescribed under Code section 409A, provided that the individual is an Eligible Employee on such date

question: What is the date by which Restoration Deferral and Base Pay Deferral Elections that apply to Base Pay earned in 2023 will become irrevocable?
answer: Restoration Deferral and Base Pay Deferral Elections (including any evergreen elections) that apply to Base Pay earned in 2023 will become irrevocable no later than on December 31, 2022

question: What is the date by which Cash Incentive Deferral Elections that apply to Cash Incentive earned in 2023 will become irrevocable?
answer: Cash Incentive Deferral Elections (including any evergreen elections) that apply to Cash Incentive earned in 2023 will become irrevocable no later than on March 30, 2023

question: What is the date by which Deferral Elections with respect to a mid-year participation period will become irrevocable?
answer: Deferral Elections with respect to a mid-year participation period will become irrevocable as of the last day of the applicable mid-year Election Period

question: What is the condition for a Deferral Election to be cancelled if an Employee ceases to be an Eligible Employee prior to it becoming irrevocable?
answer: If an Employee ceases to be an Eligible Employee (e.g., due to a reclassification as other than US Executive Payroll or Separation from Service) prior to the date that any Deferral Election (including any evergreen election) has become irrevocable as described in this subsection (C), then any such Deferral Election shall be cancelled as of the date such Deferral Election would have become irrevocable if the Employee had remained an Eligible Employee

question: What is the condition for a Deferral Election to remain in effect if an Employee ceases to be an Eligible Employee after it becomes irrevocable?
answer: Once Deferral Elections become irrevocable they generally may not be modified with respect to the Plan Year, and the Compensation, to which they apply. Accordingly, if an Employee ceases to be an Eligible Employee during the Plan Year (e.g., due to a reclassification as other than US Executive Payroll or Separation from Service), then any Deferral Election that has become irrevocable as described in this subsection (C) as of the date the Employee ceases to be an Eligible Employee shall remain in effect with respect to the Plan Year and the Compensation to which such Deferral Election applies

question: What is the condition for a Participant to be permitted to cancel an existing Deferral Election with regard to a Plan Year during that Plan Year?
answer: Notwithstanding the irrevocability rule described in Section 3.3, a Participant will be permitted to cancel an existing Deferral Election with regard to a Plan Year during that Plan Year if the Participant incurs an Unforeseeable Emergency, as determined by the Administrator

question: What is the condition for a Participant to be deemed to have elected to cancel his or her Deferral Election(s) that relate to Base Pay for the remainder of the applicable Plan Year?
answer: If a Participant has elected and received a distribution due to an Unforeseeable Emergency under Section 6.1(I), the Participant will be deemed to have elected to cancel his or her Deferral Election(s) that relate to Base Pay for the remainder of the applicable Plan Year

question: What is the condition for a Deferral Election to be “evergreen”?
answer: An Eligible Employee’s Deferral Election will be “evergreen” – it will carry-over from Plan Year to Plan Year (or from a partial Plan Year to the subsequent Plan Year in the case of a mid-year enrollment) unless it is changed or cancelled in accordance with rules established by the Administrator or as otherwise provided in this Plan

question: What is the condition for an Employee who becomes Newly Eligible during a Plan Year to not be eligible to make Participant Deferrals during such Plan Year?
answer: Except as provided in this Article III, an Employee who becomes Newly Eligible during a Plan Year (including as a result of a salary increase) will not be eligible to make Participant Deferrals during such Plan Year

question: What is the condition for a Company Non-Elective Contribution to be made for a Plan Year of promotion?
answer: For any Eligible Employee promoted onto the US Executive Payroll during an applicable Plan Year, the computation of the Company Non-Elective Contribution for the Plan Year of promotion will take into consideration any eligible pay that (i) was paid prior to the Eligible Employee’s promotion and (ii) would have been used to compute such Eligible Employee’s special 2% non-elective contribution in accordance with the terms of the Boeing 401(k), if any, but for such promotion, in accordance with the rules established by the Administrator

question: What is the condition for a Restoration True-Up Contribution to be made only if the Employee otherwise satisfies the eligibility requirements?
answer: A Restoration True-Up Contribution will be made only if the Employee otherwise satisfies the eligibility requirements for a true-up matching contribution in the Boeing 401(k)

question: What is the condition for a Restoration Matching Contribution to be made?
answer: A Participant who defers Base Pay pursuant to a Restoration Deferral Election under Section 3.3 will be credited with a Restoration Matching Contribution from the Company related to such Restoration Deferrals

question: What is the condition for a Restoration Matching Contribution to be credited to a Participant’s Account?
answer: Restoration Matching Contributions will be credited to the Participant’s Account on the date that the underlying Restoration Deferrals are credited to the Participant’s Account

question: What is the condition for a Restoration True-Up Contribution to be credited to a Participant’s Account?
answer: The Restoration True-Up Contribution, if any, will be credited to the Participant’s Account on the date that true-up matching contributions are made to the Boeing 401(k), or as soon thereafter administratively feasible

question: What is the condition for an Incentive Matching Contribution to be credited to a Participant’s Account?
answer: Incentive Matching Contributions will be credited to the Participant’s Account on the date that the underlying Cash Incentive Deferrals are credited to the Participant’s Account

question: What is the condition for a Company Non-Elective Contribution to be credited to an Eligible Employee’s Account?
answer: A Company Non-Elective Contribution will be credited to the Eligible Employee’s Account on the date the related non-elective contribution is made to the Boeing 401(k) (if any) or on the date otherwise determined by the Compensation Committee or its delegates, or, in each case, as soon thereafter as administratively feasible

question: What is the condition for a Deferral Election to be made in accordance with rules established by the Administrator?
answer: An Eligible Employee’s Deferral Election(s) must be made in accordance with rules established by the Administrator

question: What is the condition for an Eligible Employee to make separate Extra Deferral Elections with respect to Base Pay, Cash Incentive and Performance Awards?
answer: Eligible Employees may make new Deferral Elections for each succeeding Plan Year. An Eligible Employee’s Deferral Election will be “evergreen” – it will carry-over from Plan Year to Plan Year (or from a partial Plan Year to the subsequent Plan Year in the case of a mid-year enrollment) unless it is changed or cancelled in accordance with rules established by the Administrator or as otherwise provided in this Plan

question: What is the condition for an Eligible Employee to make a separate Restoration Deferral Election with respect to Base Pay?
answer: Eligible Employees may make separate Extra Deferral Elections with respect to Base Pay, Cash Incentive and Performance Awards (if any) and/or a separate Restoration Deferral Election with respect to Base Pay, each to the extent described in Section 3.1 or 3.2, as applicable

question: What is the condition for a Deferral Election to be made with respect to a full Plan Year?
answer: Deferral Elections with respect to a full Plan Year (including Cash Incentive Deferral Elections) will generally become irrevocable as of the date established by the Administrator, which in all cases shall be no later than the dates prescribed under Code section 409A, provided that the individual is an Eligible Employee on such date

question: What is the condition for a Deferral Election to be made with respect to a mid-year participation period?
answer: Deferral Elections with respect to a mid-year participation period will become irrevocable as of the last day of the applicable mid-year Election Period

question: What is the condition for a Deferral Election to be made with respect to a partial Plan Year?
answer: An Eligible Employee’s Deferral Election will be “evergreen” – it will carry-over from Plan Year to Plan Year (or from a partial Plan Year to the subsequent Plan Year in the case of a mid-year enrollment) unless it

question: What is the definition of a "group-acquired employee"?
answer: An employee of the Company who became such as an immediate or ultimate result of a merger to which the Company was a party, or of the acquisition by the Company of all or part of the assets, businesses or capital stock of another corporation or firm.

question: When will a contribution be paid for a group-acquired employee?
answer: No contribution will be paid prior to January 1, 2009.

question: When will a laid off employee be treated as a rehire if they commence a retirement benefit during a six-year period?
answer: A laid off Employee who commences a retirement benefit during this six-year period will be treated as a rehire if he or she later rehires to the Controlled Group.

question: What is the maximum period for which a supplemental percentage credited under the DC SERP contribution will be contributed?
answer: For a period not to exceed seven years.

question: When does the seven-year period for the supplemental percentage in the DC SERP contribution commence?
answer: The seven-year period will commence on January 1, 2016 (or on January 1 of the year in which the Participant attains age 55, or on the date of promotion to the US Executive Payroll, whichever is latest).

question: What is the Contribution Credit for a Participant at level EV as of a pay period prior to August 15, 2022?
answer: 2%, for a Participant at level EV (referred to as level E-2 or E-3 prior to August 15, 2022).

question: What is the Contribution Credit for a Participant at level EL as of a pay period prior to August 15, 2022?
answer: 4%, for a Participant at level EL (referred to as level E-1 prior to August 15, 2022).

question: What is the Contribution Credit for a Participant hired before January 1, 2009?
answer: The Contribution Credit will equal the sum of (i) and, if applicable, (ii): (1) 5% and (2) for a Participant who has attained age 55 (or will attain age 55 by the end of a Plan Year), 0.5% times the Participant’s whole years of Benefit Service, subject to the limitation herein.

question: What is the maximum age for a Participant to qualify for the supplemental percentage in the DC SERP contribution?
answer: Age 55.

question: What is the minimum years of Benefit Service required for a Participant to qualify for the supplemental percentage in the DC SERP contribution?
answer: The supplemental percentage is available for a Participant who has attained age 55 (or will attain age 55 by the end of a Plan Year).

question: What is the one-time contribution amount for a Participant first promoted to a level of EL or EV during a Plan Year prior to August 15, 2022?
answer: The product of (a) 2%, (b) the sum of the Participant’s Base Pay Rate in effect immediately following the promotion and his or her Cash Incentive target percentage multiplied by the Base Pay Rate, both as in effect immediately following the promotion, and (c) the Participant’s whole years of Service as of the date of first promotion to a level of EL or EV.

question: What is the condition for a Participant to be eligible for a one-time contribution under the DC SERP?
answer: An Employee who satisfies the requirements described in Section 4.5(A)(i) (Hired Between January 1, 2009 and December 31, 2019), and who is first promoted to a level of EL or EV (from a position at a level of ED) during the Plan Year (prior to August 15, 2022, first promoted to a level of E-1 through E-3 (from a position at a level of E-4 or E-5) during the Plan Year).

question: When is the one-time contribution credited to a Participant’s Account?
answer: As of the date of first promotion to a level of EL or EV (referred to as level E-1, E-2, or E-3 prior to August 15, 2022), or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible.

question: What is the condition for a Participant to be ineligible for any further contributions under the one-time contribution subsection?
answer: A Participant who has received a one-time contribution under this Section upon promotion to a level of EL or EV (referred to as level E-1, E-2, or E-3 prior to August 15, 2022), will be ineligible for any further contributions under this subsection (C)(ii).

question: What is the vesting rule for a Participant hired between January 1, 2009 and December 31, 2019 under the DC SERP?
answer: A Participant described in Section 4.5(A)(i) (Hired Between January 1, 2009 and December 31, 2019) will vest 100% in his or her DC SERP Account component(s) covered under this subsection (A) on the date the Participant satisfies the conditions in any of (i), (ii) or (iii) below.

question: What is the condition for vesting in the DC SERP for a Participant hired between January 1, 2009 and December 31, 2019 due to being on the US Executive Payroll?
answer: The Participant has been on the US Executive Payroll at a level of EL or EV (referred to as level E-1, E-2, or E-3 prior to August 15, 2022), for a period of 36 consecutive months.

question: What is the condition for vesting in the DC SERP for a Participant hired between January 1, 2009 and December 31, 2019 due to death?
answer: The Participant dies while an Employee.

question: What is the condition for vesting in the DC SERP for a Participant hired between January 1, 2009 and December 31, 2019 due to layoff?
answer: The Participant is laid off from a position at level EL or EV (referred to as level E-1, E-2, or E-3 prior to August 15, 2022]), and is eligible for benefits under The Boeing Company Executive Layoff Benefits Plan.

question: What is the vesting rule for a Participant hired before January 1, 2009 under the DC SERP?
answer: A Participant described in Section 4.5(A)(ii) (Hired Before January 1, 2009) will vest 100% in his or her DC SERP Account component covered under this subsection (B) on the date the Participant satisfies the conditions in any of (i), (ii) or (iii) below.

question: What is the condition for vesting in the DC SERP for a Participant hired before January 1, 2009 due to being on the US Executive Payroll?
answer: The Participant has been on the US Executive Payroll for a period of 36 consecutive months.

question: What is the condition for vesting in the DC SERP for a Participant hired before January 1, 2009 due to death?
answer: The Participant is fully vested under the PVP and/or BSS Plan, as applicable, and dies while an Employee before his or her DC SERP Account commences payment under this Plan.

question: What is the condition for vesting in the DC SERP for a Participant hired before January 1, 2009 due to layoff?
answer: The Participant is laid off from an US Executive position and is eligible for benefits under The Boeing Company Executive Layoff Benefits Plan.

question: What is the special vesting rule for a Participant hired between January 1, 2009 and December 31, 2019 who has attained age 55 with 10 years of Service?
answer: This Participant will be 100% vested in the portion of his or her DC SERP Account described in Section 4.5(C)(i) (Payroll Contributions) after he or she has been on the US Executive Payroll for a period of 36 consecutive months.

question: What is the special vesting rule for a Participant hired between January 1, 2009 and December 31, 2019 who has attained age 62 with one year of Service?
answer: This Participant will be 100% vested in the portion of his or her DC SERP Account described in Section 4.5(C)(i) (Payroll Contributions) after he or she has been on the US Executive Payroll for a period of 36 consecutive months.

question: What is the ratably vesting rate for a Participant hired between January 1, 2009 and December 31, 2019 in the portion of their DC SERP Account described in Section 4.5(C)(ii) (One-Time Contribution)?
answer: The Participant will vest ratably in the portion of his or her DC SERP Account described in Section 4.5(C)(ii) (One-Time Contribution), if any, at the rate of 1/36 for each consecutive month that the Participant is on the US Executive Payroll at a level of EL or EV (referred to as level E-1, E-2, or E-3 prior to August 15, 2022).

question: When does the ratably vesting rule for the one-time contribution begin?
answer: Starting with the date on which the Participant was first promoted to the US Executive Payroll at a level of EL or EV (referred to as level E-1, E-2, or E-3 prior to August 15, 2022).

question: What is the condition for an Authorized Period of Absence to count toward vesting?
answer: An Authorized Period of Absence from the US Executive Payroll will count as a period on the US Executive Payroll, and an Authorized Period of Absence from a position at level EL or EV (referred to as level E-1, E-2, or E-3 prior to August 15, 2022) will count as a period at these levels.

question: What happens if an Employee ceases to be at the applicable level for any reason other than an Authorized Period of Absence and later returns to a position at the applicable level?
answer: These non-consecutive periods of service will not be aggregated for purposes of determining whether the 36-consecutive month requirement has been met.

question: What is the condition for uninterrupted service at ULA or USA to be credited toward the 36 consecutive months requirements for a Participant transferring from the Controlled Group to ULA or USA?
answer: Uninterrupted service at ULA or USA as an executive in a position at a comparable level will be credited toward the 36 consecutive months requirements described herein, provided that the Participant transfers directly from the US Executive Payroll (or a position at level EL or EV (referred to as level E-1, E-2, or E-3 prior to August 15, 2022), if applicable) at the Controlled Group to comparable executive status at ULA or USA, as applicable.

question: What is the condition for uninterrupted service at ULA or USA to not be credited toward vesting for a Participant transferring from ULA or USA to the Controlled Group?
answer: ULA and USA service will not be credited toward vesting under this Plan for any period following the Participant’s removal from this executive status.

question: What is the time period during which a Participant’s service at ULA or USA will be credited toward the 36 consecutive months requirements for vesting?
answer: Uninterrupted service at ULA or USA as an executive in a position at a comparable level will be credited toward the 36 consecutive months requirements described herein, provided that the Participant transfers directly from the US Executive Payroll (or a position at level EL or EV (referred to as level E-1, E-2, or E-3 prior to August 15, 2022), if applicable) at the Controlled Group to comparable executive status at ULA or USA, as applicable.

question: What is the condition under which service at ULA or USA will not be credited toward vesting for a Participant who transfers from the Controlled Group to ULA or USA?
answer: ULA and USA service will not be credited toward vesting under this Plan for any period following the Participant’s removal from this executive status.

question: What is the condition under which service at ULA or USA will not be credited toward vesting for a Participant who transfers from ULA or USA to the Controlled Group?
answer: ULA and USA service will not be credited toward vesting under this Plan for any period prior to the Participant’s attainment of this executive status at ULA or USA, as applicable.

question: What happens to a Participant’s nonvested portion of their DC SERP Account if they separate from service before becoming 100% vested in the payroll contribution portion?
answer: The Participant will forfeit all rights to the nonvested portion of his or her DC SERP Account attributable to the period prior to his or her Separation from Service or transfer.

question: What happens to a Participant’s DC SERP Account accrued after resuming service if they had previously stopped accruing service due to a Separation from Service and were partially vested in the one-time contribution portion?
answer: The DC SERP Account accrued after such resumption will not be vested until the Participant satisfies the requirements of subsection (A) or (C) above following such resumption.

question: How many separate vesting requirements apply to a Participant’s DC SERP Account components?
answer: Separate vesting requirements apply to each component of a Participant’s DC SERP Account described in Sections 4.4(C)(i)(a), (i)(b), and (ii).

question: What happens to a Participant’s vesting status in a DC SERP Account component if they separate from service after becoming 100% vested in that component?
answer: The Participant will be fully vested in any additional accruals under the same DC SERP Account component following rehire or return (even if the Participant fails to be at the applicable pay level for 36 consecutive months following rehire or return).

question: What happens to a Participant’s vesting status in a different DC SERP Account component after separating from service?
answer: The Participant will not be fully vested in any amounts accrued under a different DC SERP Account component unless and until the corresponding applicable vesting requirements under this Section 5.5 otherwise have been satisfied.

question: What is one circumstance under which a Participant may forfeit any part or all of his or her DC SERP Account?
answer: The Participant is convicted of a felony involving theft, fraud, embezzlement, or other similar unlawful acts against the Controlled Group or against the Controlled Group’s interests.

question: What does “engaging in competition” include under the forfeiture provisions of the Plan?
answer: “Engaging in competition” shall include but is not limited to representing, providing services to, or being an employee of or associated in a business capacity with, any person or entity that is engaged, directly or indirectly, in competition with any Controlled Group business or that takes a position adverse to any Controlled Group business, regardless of the position or duties the Participant takes, in such a manner that is determined to be detrimental to, prejudicial to or in conflict with the interests of the Controlled Group, all as determined by the Administrator in its sole discretion.

question: What is one circumstance under which a Participant may forfeit any part or all of his or her DC SERP Account involving actions against employees?
answer: The Participant, without the advance approval of The Boeing Company’s Senior Vice President of Human Resources (or equivalent but for title), induces or attempts to induce, directly or indirectly, any of the Controlled Group’s employees, representatives or consultants to terminate, discontinue or cease working with or for the Controlled Group, or to breach any contract with the Controlled Group, in order to work with or for, or enter into a contract with, the Participant or any third party.

question: What is one circumstance under which a Participant may forfeit any part or all of his or her DC SERP Account involving statements about the Controlled Group?
answer: The Participant disparages or otherwise makes any statements about the Controlled Group, its products, or its employees that could be in any way viewed as negative or critical.

question: What is one circumstance under which a Participant may forfeit any part or all of his or her DC SERP Account involving use of proprietary information?
answer: With respect to contributions made to the Plan on and after January 1, 2017, the Participant uses or discloses proprietary or confidential information, including but not limited to trade secrets, of the Controlled Group.

question: What is the minimum age requirement for a Participant to receive a lump sum distribution under the installment payment option?
answer: The lump sum distribution option is a single lump sum payment that will be made in the later of: (i) January of the first Plan Year following Separation from Service, or (ii) January of the first Plan Year following the Participant’s attainment of a specified age (subject to subsection (E) below), as elected by the Participant under this Section 6.1.

question: What is the range of years for which installment payments can be elected under the Plan?
answer: The installment payment option is a series of annual installment payments for a period between 2 and 15 years, as elected by the Participant under this Section 6.1.

question: When do annual installment payments begin under the Plan?
answer: Annual installment payments, if elected, will begin in the later of: (i) January of the first Plan Year following Separation from Service, or (ii) January of the first Plan Year following the Participant’s attainment of a specified age (subject to (E) below), as elected by the Participant under this Section 6.1.

question: What happens to a Participant’s remaining Account balance if it is $10,000 or less upon any scheduled payment date for an installment payment?
answer: Subject to the six-month delay in payment for Specified Employees under subsection (H), if a Participant has elected to receive installments and his or her remaining Account balance is $10,000 or less upon any scheduled payment date (excluding the balance of the DCP Account), the entire remaining balance will be paid as one final installment payment at that time.

question: What is the requirement for changing a distribution election after the initial election is made?
answer: A Participant may change a distribution election (or deemed election) after the initial distribution election becomes effective (or deemed effective) only once with regard to each of the following subaccounts: the Participant’s Restoration Account, Executive Benefit Account, Extra Deferral Account, and DCP Account (Deferrals) and DCP Account (Match).

question: What must a new distribution election provide for in order to be effective?
answer: The new distribution election must provide for an additional deferral period of at least 5 years beyond the original distribution date.

question: When must a new distribution election be submitted to be effective?
answer: A new distribution election must be submitted in accordance with the rules prescribed by the Administrator at least 12 months before the existing scheduled distribution date under the applicable subaccount.

question: How long must a revised distribution election wait before it takes effect?
answer: The revised distribution election must not take effect for at least 12 months after it is made.

question: Can installment payments be changed or revoked once they have begun?
answer: In no event can installment payments be changed or revoked once they have begun.

question: When are payments made under the distribution options?
answer: Payments will be made in January (subject to subsection (H)).

question: When do benefits under the Plan begin for a Participant who attains age 70½ and separates from service?
answer: Payment of benefits under this Plan will begin no later than the first January following the calendar year in which the Participant both attains (or would have attained) age 70½ and is Separated from Service.

question: When do benefits begin for a Participant who is actively employed beyond age 70½?
answer: Payment of benefits for Participants actively employed beyond age 70½ will begin no later than the first January following the calendar year in which the Participant Separates from Service.

question: What is the waiting period for a Specified Employee before receiving a distribution under the Plan?
answer: A Specified Employee will not receive any distribution under this Plan during the six-month period immediately following his or her Separation from Service.

question: When does a Specified Employee’s distribution begin?
answer: This distribution will be made or commence as of the latest of: (1) the time elected (or deemed elected) under subsection (A), (B), or (C), as applicable, (2) the month following completion of the six-month waiting period (for Specified Employees who Separate from Service between July 1 and December 31), and (3) January of the first Plan Year following Separation from Service (for Specified Employees who Separate from Service between January 1 and June 30).

question: What happens if a Specified Employee dies during the six-month waiting period?
answer: In the event of a Specified Employee’s death during the six-month waiting period, the waiting period will cease to apply. The Specified Employee’s benefits will be distributed in accordance with Section 6.2 (Death Benefits) below.

question: What is the form of distribution for a Participant’s Executive Benefit Account?
answer: A Participant is deemed to have elected to receive his or her Executive Benefit Account in a lump sum, payable in January of the first Plan Year following Separation from Service (subject to subsection (H)).

question: What is the form of distribution for a Participant’s Restoration Account if no timely election is made?
answer: If a Participant fails to make a timely election with regard to the timing of payment of his or her Restoration Account, then the Participant will be deemed to have elected to receive payment in January of the first Plan Year following the Participant’s Separation from Service (subject to subsection (H)).

question: What is the form of distribution for a Participant’s Extra Deferral Account if no timely election is made?
answer: If a Participant fails to make a timely election with regard to the form of payment of his or her Extra Deferral Account, then the Participant will be deemed to have elected to receive payment in a lump sum.

question: What is the form of distribution for a Participant’s Extra Deferral Account if a timely election is not made regarding timing?
answer: If a Participant fails to make a timely election with regard to the timing of payment of his or her Extra Deferral Account, then the Participant will be deemed to have elected to receive payment in January of the first Plan Year following the Participant’s Separation from Service (subject to subsection (H)).

question: What is the form of distribution for a Participant’s Restoration Account if a timely election is not made regarding form?
answer: If a Participant fails to make a timely election with regard to the form of payment of his or her Restoration Account, then the Participant will be deemed to have elected to receive payment in a lump sum.

question: What is the requirement for changing a distribution election for a Participant who is not an Eligible Employee?
answer: If the election change is made by an Eligible Employee outside of the annual enrollment period or at any time by a Participant who is not an Eligible Employee, such election change will be irrevocable when made.

question: What is the requirement for changing a distribution election made during the annual enrollment period?
answer: If an election change is made by an Eligible Employee during the annual enrollment period, it can be changed during such period and the last change on file (if any) as of the end of the annual enrollment period will be irrevocable.

question: What is the requirement for a distribution election change that would defer commencement beyond age 70½ and Separation from Service?
answer: To the extent any such changes would defer commencement of any portion of the Participant’s Restoration Account, Executive Benefit Account, Extra Deferral Account or DCP Account beyond both age 70½ and Separation from Service, the changes will not be effective.

question: What is the valuation date used to determine the amount of a distribution made other than in January?
answer: For payments occurring other than in January, the amount of the distribution will be determined based on the value of the Participant’s Account as of the first business day of the month that payment will be made (or such other distribution valuation date as is specified by the Administrator).

question: What is the maximum number of years for which installment payments can be made?
answer: The installment payment option is a series of annual installment payments for a period between 2 and 15 years, as elected by the Participant under this Section 6.1.

question: What is the minimum number of years for which installment payments can be made?
answer: The installment payment option is a series of annual installment payments for a period between 2 and 15 years, as elected by the Participant under this Section 6.1.

question: What is the minimum deferral period required for a new distribution election to be effective?
answer: The new distribution election must provide for an additional deferral period of at least 5 years beyond the original distribution date.

question: What is the earliest time a distribution can begin for a Participant who separates from service?
answer: The lump sum distribution option is a single lump sum payment that will be made in the later of: (i) January of the first Plan Year following Separation from Service, or (ii) January of the first Plan Year following the Participant’s attainment of a specified age (subject to subsection (E) below), as elected by the Participant under this Section 6.1.

question: What is the earliest time a distribution can begin for a Participant who attains age 70½ and separates from service?
answer: Payment of benefits under this Plan will begin no later than the first January following the calendar year in which the Participant both attains (or would have attained) age 70½ and is Separated from Service.

question: What is the earliest time a distribution can begin for a Participant who is actively employed beyond age 70½?
answer: Payment of benefits for Participants actively employed beyond age 70½ will begin no later than the first January following the calendar year in which the Participant Separates from Service.

question: What is the earliest time a distribution can begin for a Specified Employee who separates from service between January 1 and June 30?
